title: Impact of local air pressure on ion mobilities and data consistency in diaPASEF-based high throughput proteomics
projectDescription: Data-independent acquisition (DIA) on ion mobility – TOF hybrid mass spectrometers enables deep proteome coverage and high data completeness in large-scale proteomics studies. For advanced acquisition schemes such as parallel accumulation serial fragmentation-based DIA (diaPASEF) stability of ion mobility (1/K0) over time is crucial for consistent data quality. We found that minor changes in environmental air pressure systematically affect vacuum pressure in the TIMS analyzer, causing ion mobility shifts. By comparing experimental ion mobilities with historical weather data, we attributed observed drifts to daily fluctuations in ground air pressure. These drifts negatively impact peptide quantification across consecutively acquired samples due to drift-dependent abundance changes and increased missing values for ions located at the boundaries of diaPASEF isolation windows, which cannot be corrected by post-processing. To address this, we applied an in-batch mobility autocalibration feature on a run-wise basis, leading to full elimination of ion mobility drifts.
sampleProcessingProtocol: -The 96 samples impacted by ion mobility drift were derived from a cysteine activity-based protein-protein profiling study in THP1 cells. Preparation was conducted as described previously (10.1038/s41587-020-00778-3).  -The 192 samples analyzed with in-batch calibration originated from a proteomics study in HCT116 cells. Briefly, cell pellets were subjected to acetone precipitation (80% acetone) for 2 hours at -20°C. After removing the supernatant, the samples were dried, and proteins were digested overnight at room temperature using trypsin. For the sample load variation study, a commercial HeLa digest (Pierce) was reconstituted in 0.05% TFA and diluted to achieve sample loads of 50ng, 100 ng, 200 ng, 400 ng, 800 ng, and 1.6 µg. -Samples were loaded onto EvoTips (EvoSep) according to vendor recommendations before LC/MS analysis. LC-MS/MS analysis: -Peptides were separated on the Evosep One LC system (EvoSep) with Pepsep C18 columns, using the manufacturer’s predefined methods (denoted by samples per day “SPD”), and analyzed on the timsTOFpro 2 mass spectrometer connected to a Captiva ion source (Bruker). -Samples from cysteine activity-based protein profiling were analyzed using the 30 SPD method, and a diaPASEF acquisition scheme optimized by the py_diAID software (10.1016/j.mcpro.2022.100279.).  -The 192 proteomics samples and the “variable load” Hela samples were analyzed using the 60 SPD method and  the diaPASEF “high speed” scheme, as previously described (10.1038/s41592-020-00998-0). -For in-batch mobility calibration, three vendor-recommended mass calibrants were used: m/z 622 (0.9917 Vs/cm², Hexakis(2,2-difluoroethoxy)phosphazene, Apollo Scientific), m/z 922 (1.1984 Vs/cm², Hexakis(2,2,3,3- tetrafluoropropoxy)phosphazene, Apollo Scientific), and m/z 1222 (1.3934 Vs/cm², Chip Cube high mass reference HP-1221, Agilent Technologies). In-batch calibration was activated and saved in the acquisition method using timsControl version 5.0.9. To ensure robust detection of the calibrants during automated calibration, the mobility range was set to 1/K0 of 0.7–1.6.
dataProcessingProtocol: For the cysteine activity-based protein profiling a ddaPASEF-based project-specific library was generated by FragPipe 19 (10.1038/s41467-022-31492-0). For the 192 sample study and the “variable sample load” study an in silico library was predicted by DIA-NN 1.8.1 with default settings using a FASTA swissprot download from 2018. diaPASEF raw data was analyzed using DIA-NN 1.8.1 (10.1038/s41592-019-0638-x) with both MS1- and MS2 mass tolerance at 15 ppm and a scan window of10. Other settings were default.
